label: ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy Expert Panel Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Variant Interpretation Guidelines for DNAH5 Version 1.0

criteriaCodes.description: Patient’s phenotype or family history is highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   To meet PP4\_Moderate, the proband must have genotyping by exome sequencing, genome sequencing, or next-generation sequencing-based primary ciliary dyskinesia panel, plus copy number variation analysis, showing absence of biallelic variants from all other primary ciliary dyskinesia loci associated with outer dynein arm defects or outer + inner dynein arm defects. At the minimum, the loci genotyped must have included; _DNAI1_, _CCDC103_, _DNAI2_, _ODAD4/TTC25_, _ODAD1/CCDC114_, _CCDC151/ODAD3_, _ODAD2/ARMC4_, and _DNAH9_. Ideally, this list would also include _DNAL1_, _CLXN/ODAD5_, _LRRC56_, and _TXNDC3/NME8_, however, genotyping of these rarer causes of primary ciliary dyskinesia with outer dynein arm or outer + inner dynein arm defects is not required.
*   The proband must also have well-characterized primary ciliary dyskinesia (defined by greater than or equal to 6 phenotype points). Please see the attached PP4 table for calculation of phenotype points.
*   The proband must also have an outer dynein arm defect (defined as electron microscopy showing ciliary ultrastructure with absent / shortened / reduced number of outer dynein arms, or by DNAH5 / DNAI1 / DNAI2  immunofluorescence showing its absence from the ciliary axonemes).
*   Please note that although DNAH5-associated cases have outer dynein defects specifically, inner dynein arms can be difficult to detect due to lower electronic density, so an additional "inner dynein arm defect” does not disqualify a proband from PP4 consideration.
*   Please note that missense variants are not always associated with absence of DNAH5 immunofluorescence from the ciliary axoneme, so a negative result in this test does not disqualify a proband from PP4 consideration.

criteriaCodes.label: PP4

criteriaCodes.description:
De novo (both maternity and paternity confirmed) in a patient with the disease and no family history.
Note: Confirmation of paternity only is insufficient. Egg donation, surrogate motherhood, errors in embryo transfer, etc. can contribute to non-maternity.

evidenceStrengths.description:
PS2 is considered when the patient harbors the variant in the _de novo_ state with no family history of disease and maternity and paternity have been confirmed (for example by trio testing based on exome sequencing / genome sequencing).

*   Strength level is determined using ClinGen SVI’s recommended point system (see attached table).
*   Use the number of points from the first row in Table 1 (“phenotype highly specific for DNAH5”) if the proband has 6 or more points according to the attached PP4 Table from clinical features consistent with primary ciliary dyskinesia including confirmation of an outer dynein arm defect by either electron microscopy or immunofluorescence, and genotyping by whole exome sequencing, next-generation sequencing-based PCD panel, OR whole genome sequencing, plus copy number variation analysis, showing absence of biallelic variants from the following PCD loci associated with ODA or ODA + IDA defects; DNAI1, CCDC103, DNAI2, ODAD4/TTC25, ODAD1/CCDC114, CCDC151/ODAD3, ODAD2/ARMC4, and DNAH9.
*   Use the number of points from the second row in Table 1 (“phenotype consistent with DNAH5 but not highly specific”) if the proband has 6 or more points according to the attached PP4 Table from clinical features consistent with primary ciliary dyskinesia including confirmation of an outer dynein arm defect by either electron microscopy or immunofluorescence.
*   Use the number of points from the third row in Table 1 (“phenotype consistent with DNAH5 but not highly specific and high genetic heterogeneity”) if the proband has clinical features consistent with primary ciliary dyskinesia but no confirmation of an outer dynein arm defect by either electron microscopy or immunofluorescence.
*   Since _DNAH5_ is associated with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance, if a second variant is not identified in addition to the _de novo_ variant, decrease the strength of evidence by one level, or consider the possibility to avoid including the proband in PS2 or PM6 altogether.

criteriaCodes.label: PS2

criteriaCodes.description:
Lack of segregation in affected members of a family.
Caveat: The presence of phenocopies for common phenotypes (i.e. cancer, epilepsy) can mimic lack of segregation among affected individuals. Also, families may have more than one pathogenic variant contributing to an autosomal dominant disorder, further confounding an apparent lack of segregation.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Met by 1 affected family member without the variant.
*   In order to be considered “affected” the family member must have; (1) An electron microscopy result showing a structural defect consistent with proband, or (2) situs inversus, or (3) wet cough from \<6 months of age combined with either chronic nasal congestion / neonatal respiratory distress / laterality defect, or (4) bronchiectasis combined with either chronic nasal congestion / neonatal respiratory distress / laterality defect.
*   For consanguineous families, consider avoiding this code if the family is suspected to have two separate causes of PCD.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: BS4

criteriaCodes.description: A synonymous variant for which splicing prediction algorithms predict no impact to the splice consensus sequence nor the creation of a new splice site AND the nucleotide is not highly conserved.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   BP7 is met by a synonymous variant if SpliceAI does not predict a splicing defect (all SpliceAI delta scores lower than the cutoff of \<0.1).
    *   Synonymous variants in the first nucleotide of an exon or the final 3 nucleotides of an exon are not eligible for BP7, as they are considered part of the splice acceptor or splice donor region. (The position of a synonymous variant relative to the exon boundaries can be found by searching the variant at; [https://mutalyzer.nl/](https://mutalyzer.nl/).)
*   BP7 is met by an intronic variant if SpliceAI does not predict a splicing defect (all SpliceAI delta scores lower than the cutoff of \<0.1).
    *   Intronic variants between +1 and +6 or between -1 and -20 are not eligible for BP7, as they are considered part of the splice donor or splice acceptor region (PMID: 37352859).
*   Although a SpliceAI score \<0.1 will also meet BP4, the BP7 and BP4 codes can be used at the same time, as this is not considered to be double-counting (PMID: 37352859).
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PP5

criteriaCodes.description: Observed in trans with a pathogenic variant for a fully penetrant dominant gene/disorder or observed in cis with a pathogenic variant in any inheritance pattern.
criteriaCodes.label: BP2

criteriaCodes.description: Well-established in vitro or in vivo functional studies show no damaging effect on protein function or splicing.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   The attached file entitled “DNAH5\_Functional\_Assays” contains a description of all functional assays approved for use to meet the PS3 code, however, no BS3-eligible assays have yet been found in the published literature showing non-damaging effects on DNAH5.
*   Future evidence from animal models showing absence of DNAH5-related defects can meet BS3 but has not yet been found for _DNAH5_.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   The attached file entitled “DNAH5\_Functional\_Assays” contains a description of all functional assays approved for use to meet the PS3\_Supporting code, however, no BS3\_Supporting-eligible assays have yet been found in the published literature showing non-damaging effects on DNAH5. Future evidence showing a non-damaging effect on DNAH5 function can meet BS3\_Supporting but has not yet been found for _DNAH5_.
*   The VCEP considered making BS3\_Supporting applicable for patient cell assays with immunofluorescent staining of DNAH5 in ciliated cells or with electron microscopy showing absence of outer dynein arm defects in ciliary axonemes (examples found in PMID: 16627867), but pointed out that missense variants or hypomorphs may give a “normal” result with residual protein present, or outer dynein arms only partially defective. The group decided that these patient cell-based experiments should be included in the patient phenotype (PP4 code).
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: BS3

criteriaCodes.description: Observed in a healthy adult individual for a recessive (homozygous), dominant (heterozygous), or X-linked (hemizygous) disorder, with full penetrance expected at an early age.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Met if the variant is present in a homozygote examined in a clinical setting without any features of the phenotype (respiratory disease or situs defects).
*   Met by greater than or equal to 3 homozygotes in gnomAD v4.1.1.
*   The rationale for requiring at least 3 homozygotes is based on known examples of disease-causing variants with up to 1 homozygote in gnomAD.
*   Additional care is taken in considering homozygotes from bottlenecked populations, and these are discussed on a case-by-case basis.
*   The group has expressed some concern about the possibility of hypomorphic variants causing disease but still meeting this criterion.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: BS2

criteriaCodes.description: Protein length changes due to in-frame deletions/insertions in a non-repeat region or stop-loss variants.

evidenceStrengths.description:
Protein length changes due to in-frame deletions/insertions in a non-repeat region or stop-loss variants.

*   Met at default strength (PM4) by an in-frame **deletion** resulting in a protein length change **greater than or equal to 2 amino acids,** if at least one of the deleted amino acids is highly conserved (PhyloP >2.0).
*   Met at default strength (PM4) by an in-frame **insertion** resulting in a protein length change **greater than or equal to 2 amino acids**, if at least one of the adjacent amino acids is highly conserved (PhyloP >2.0).
*   PM4 is mutually exclusive with PVS1 and PP3 (in order not to double-count _in silico_ predictor data) but can be used together with PM1.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
Protein length changes due to in-frame deletions/insertions in a non-repeat region or stop-loss variants.

*   Met at reduced strength (PM4\_Supporting) for an in-frame **deletion** resulting in a protein length change of **1 amino acid**, if at least one of the deleted amino acids is highly conserved (PhyloP >2.0).
*   Met at reduced strength (PM4\_Supporting) for an in-frame i**nsertion** resulting in a protein length change of **1 amino acid**, if at least one of the adjacent amino acids is highly conserved (PhyloP >2.0).
*   Met at reduced strength (PM4\_Supporting) by a **stop-loss** variant predicted to extend the C-terminus of DNAH5 by additional amino acids.
*   PM4 is mutually exclusive with PVS1 and PP3 (in order not to double-count _in silico_ predictor data) but can be used together with PM1.
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PM4

criteriaCodes.description:
The prevalence of the variant in affected individuals is significantly increased compared to the prevalence in controls.
Note 1: Relative risk (RR) or odds ratio (OR), as obtained from case-control studies, is >5.0 and the confidence interval around the estimate of RR or OR does not include 1.0. See manuscript for detailed guidance.
Note 2: In instances of very rare variants where case-control studies may not reach statistical significance, the prior observation of the variant in multiple unrelated patients with the same phenotype, and its absence in controls, may be used as moderate level of evidence.

criteriaCodes.description: Assumed de novo, but without confirmation of paternity and maternity.

criteriaCodes.label: PM6

criteriaCodes.description:
Null variant (nonsense, frameshift, canonical +/−1 or 2 splice sites, initiation codon, single or multi-exon deletion) in a gene where loss of function (LOF) is a known mechanism of disease.
Caveats:
 * Beware of genes where LOF is not a known disease mechanism (e.g. GFAP, MYH7).
 * Use caution interpreting LOF variants at the extreme 3’ end of a gene.
 * Use caution with splice variants that are predicted to lead to exon skipping but leave the remainder of the protein intact.
 * Use caution in the presence of multiple transcripts.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Use the modified ClinGen SVI recommended flow chart diagram when assessing LOF variants.
*   Apply PVS1 at the default (very strong) level for nonsense or frameshift variants that introduce a premature stop codon between codons 2 and 4557, as nonsense-mediated decay is predicted..
*   Apply PVS1 to a canonical splice site variant only if SpliceAI predicts an impact on splicing (an exception is known in another PCD-related gene, _DNAH11_). At least one SpliceAI score must be greater than or equal to 0.2 (PMID: 37352859). However, PP3 should not be applied, as this code is mutually exclusive with PVS1.
*   Apply PVS1 at the default (very strong) level for canonical splice variants predicted to skip one of the following exons, which would shift frame if skipped; 3, 4, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 35, 36, 37, 41, 43, 45, 46, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 62, 63, 66, 67, 68, 69, 72, 73, 78, or 79.
*   Apply PVS1 at the default (very strong) level for canonical splice variants predicted to skip one of the following exons, which contain at least one site where a missense variant has been reported pathogenic; 38, 48, or 60.
*   Apply PVS1 at the default (very strong) level for canonical splice variants predicted to skip one of the following exons, which would preserve frame if skipped, but encode one of the AAA regions that make up the motor domain = 39, 40, 42, 44, 47, 64, 65, or 71.
*   If a missense, synonymous, or intronic variant outside of the canonical splice sites has a SpliceAI score greater than or equal to 0.2 and has been confirmed to cause complete or near-complete disruption of splicing within the mRNA in a study of patient RNA or minigene assay, avoid PP3 and PS3\_Supporting and evaluate PVS1 instead (PMID: 37352859).
*   Apply PVS1 at the default (very strong) level for initiation codon (start loss) variants, as the second in-frame ATG does not occur until codon 81 and it is not clear whether it can function as an alternative transcription start site.
*   Apply PVS1 at the default (very strong) level for deletion variants when the truncated/altered region is out of frame and predicted to trigger NMD (including single-exon deletions of exon 3, 4, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 35, 36, 37, 41, 43, 45, 46, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 62, 63, 66, 67, 68, 69, 72, or 73) or critical to protein function (including single exon deletions of exon 38, 39, 40, 42, 44, 47, 48, 64, 65, or 71, encoding part of an AAA domain, exon 58, 59, 60, or 61, which encode part of the stalk domain, or exon 78, which contains known pathogenic missense variants, or exon 1, which contains the start codon and 5'UTR).
*   Apply PVS1 for duplication variants if the duplication is either proximal in tandem and disrupts frame, or internal (in tandem or not in tandem, regardless of its effect on frame).
evidenceStrengths.label: Very Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Use the modified ClinGen SVI recommended flow chart diagram when assessing LOF variants.
*   Apply PVS1\_Strong to a canonical splice site variant only if SpliceAI predicts an impact on splicing (an exception is known in another PCD-related gene, _DNAH11_). At least one SpliceAI score must be greater than or equal to 0.2 (PMID: 37352859).  However, PP3 should not be applied, as this code is mutually exclusive with PVS1.
*   Apply PVS1 at the PVS1\_Strong level for multi-exon deletion variants when the truncated/altered region has an unknown role in DNAH5 function, is in frame, and truncates more than 10% of the protein product.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Use the modified ClinGen SVI recommended flow chart diagram when assessing LOF variants.
*   Apply PVS1\_Moderate for nonsense or frameshift variants that introduce a premature stop codon between codons 4558 and 4624, as they are predicted not to result in nonsense-mediated decay, but rather to cause C-terminal truncation disrupting a region of uncertain function that represents less than 2% of the total length of the protein product.
*   Apply PVS1\_Moderate to a canonical splice site variant only if SpliceAI predicts an impact on splicing (an exception is known in another PCD-related gene, _DNAH11_). At least one SpliceAI score must be greater than or equal to 0.2 (PMID: 37352859).  However, PP3 should not be applied, as this code is mutually exclusive with PVS1.
*   Apply PVS1\_Moderate for canonical splice variants predicted to skip one of the following exons, which would preserve frame if skipped; 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 19, 25, 26, 33, 34, 58, 59, 61, 70, 74, 75, 76, or 77.
*   Apply PVS1 at the PVS1\_Moderate level for deletion variants when the truncated/altered region has an unknown role in DNAH5 function and is either in frame (including single-exon deletions of exon 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 19, 25, 26, 33, 34, 70, 74, 75, 76, or 77) or out-of-frame but not predicted to trigger NMD (including single-exon deletions of exon 79).
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

criteriaCodes.label: PVS1

criteriaCodes.description:
Multiple lines of computational evidence support a deleterious effect on the gene or gene product (conservation, evolutionary, splicing impact, etc.).
Caveat: As many in silico algorithms use the same or very similar input for their predictions, each algorithm should not be counted as an independent criterion. PP3 can be used only once in any evaluation of a variant.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Apply PP3\_Strong for any missense variant if REVEL score is greater than or equal to 0.932.
*   PP3\_Strong cannot be combined with PM1 or PM5 at any level, as the combined strength of these 3 codes is limited to the strong level.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Apply PP3\_Moderate for any missense variant if REVEL score is greater than or equal to 0.870.
*   PP3\_Moderate can be combined with PM1 and/or PM5, however, their combined strength is limited to strong. For example, a variant can meet PP3\_Moderate, PM1\_Supporting and PM5\_Supporting (which together are equivalent to 1 strong code), while a variant cannot meet PP3\_Moderate in combination with both PM1 and PM5 (since PM1 and PM5 together are already equivalent to 1 strong code).
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Apply this code at the default (PP3) strength level for any missense variant if REVEL score is greater than or equal to 0.690.
*   Use SpliceAI to apply this code at the default (PP3) strength level for any missense, synonymous, or intronic variant outside of the canonical splice sites with any SpliceAI delta score greater than or equal to 0.2.
*   PP3 cannot be met by a canonical splice site variant (evaluate for PVS1 instead).
*   If a missense, synonymous, or intronic variant outside of the canonical splice sites has a SpliceAI score greater than or equal to 0.2 and has been confirmed to cause complete or near-complete disruption of splicing within the mRNA in a study of patient RNA or minigene assay, avoid PP3 and PS3\_Supporting and evaluate PVS1 instead (PMID: 37352859).
*   PP3 can be combined with PM1 and/or PM5, however, their combined strength is limited to strong. For example, a variant can meet PP3, PM1, and PM5\_Supporting (which together are equivalent to 1 strong code), while a variant cannot meet PP3 in combination with both PM1 and PM5 (since PM1 and PM5 together are already equivalent to 1 strong code).
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PP3

criteriaCodes.description:
Novel missense change at an amino acid residue where a different missense change determined to be pathogenic has been seen before.
Example: Arg156His is pathogenic; now you observe Arg156Cys.
Caveat: Beware of changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Met at the default (PM5) level when the missense variant under evaluation has a comparison missense variant at the same residue that has reached a pathogenic classification by this VCEP’s rule specifications without using PM5.
*   The variant under evaluation must have a Grantham score equal to or higher than that of the Pathogenic comparison variant (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid_replacement#Grantham's_distance).
*   SpliceAI must be used to ensure that neither the variant of interest nor the comparison variant is predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores \<0.1) or that both the variant of interest and the comparison variant are predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores >0.2).
*   PM5 cannot be used if any variant causing the same amino acid change has previously reached a benign or likely benign classification using this VCEP’s rule specifications (not just a previous classification in ClinVar).
*   PM5 can be combined with PM1 and/or PP3, however, their combined strength is limited to strong. For example, a variant can meet PM5, PM1\_Supporting and PP3\_Supporting (which together are equivalent to 1 strong code), while a variant cannot meet PM5 in combination with PP3\_Strong.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Met at the PM5\_Supporting level when the missense variant under evaluation has a comparison missense variant at the same residue that has reached a likely pathogenic classification by this VCEP’s rule specifications without using PM5.
*   The variant under evaluation must have a Grantham score equal to or higher than that of the Likely Pathogenic comparison variant (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid_replacement#Grantham's_distance).
*   SpliceAI must be used to ensure that neither the variant of interest nor the comparison variant is predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores \<0.1) or that both the variant of interest and the comparison variant are predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores >0.2).
*   PM5\_Supporting  cannot be used if any variant causing the same amino acid change has previously reached a benign or likely benign classification using this VCEP’s rule specifications (not just a previous classification in ClinVar).
*   PM5\_Supporting can be combined with PM1 and/or PP3, however, their combined strength is limited to strong. For example, a variant can meet PM5\_Supporting, PM1\_Supporting and PP3\_Moderate (which together are equivalent to 1 strong code), while a variant cannot meet PM5 in combination with PP3\_Strong.
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PM5

criteriaCodes.description: Allele frequency is greater than expected for disorder.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Met by Grpmax filtering allele frequency greater than or equal to 0.0006 in gnomAD v4.1.1 or the most up-to-date version of gnomAD.
*   Derived by decreasing the BA1 cutoff by 10X, then adjusting to ensure that the BS1 code would not be met by high-frequency disease-causing founder variants.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

criteriaCodes.label: BS1

criteriaCodes.description:
Same amino acid change as a previously established pathogenic variant regardless of nucleotide change.
Example: Val->Leu caused by either G>C or G>T in the same codon.
Caveat: Beware of changes that impact splicing rather than at the amino acid/protein level.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   This code can be applied to a missense variant with the caveats below:
    *   Apply PS1 for a missense variant if a comparison variant encoding the same amino acid change has reached a pathogenic classification using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (not just a previous classification in ClinVar). 
    *   SpliceAI must be used to ensure that neither the missense variant under evaluation nor the comparison missense variant is predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores \<0.1), or that both the missense variant under evaluation and the comparison missense variant are predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores >0.2).
    *   PS1 cannot be applied for a missense variant if any comparison variant causing the same amino acid change has previously reached a benign or likely benign classification using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (not just a previous classification in ClinVar).
*   This code can be applied to an intronic or synonymous variant with the caveats below:
    *   Apply PS1 for a variant predicted to disrupt splicing (SpliceAI score ≥0.2, meeting PP3) that is located outside of the canonical splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions, if a comparison variant at the same nucleotide position, with the same predicted impact, has been previously classified pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
    *   Apply PS1 for a variant located within the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions (meeting PVS1) if a comparison variant located within the same splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide has been classified pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   This code can be applied to a missense variant with the caveats below:
    *   Apply PS1\_Moderate for a missense variant If a comparison variant encoding the same amino acid change has reached a likely pathogenic classification using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (not just a previous classification in ClinVar).
    *   SpliceAI must be used to ensure that neither the missense variant under evaluation nor the comparison missense variant is predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores \<0.1), or that both the missense variant under evaluation and the comparison missense variant are predicted to cause a splicing defect (SpliceAI scores >0.2).
    *   PS1 cannot be applied for a missense variant if any comparison variant causing the same amino acid change has previously reached a benign or likely benign classification using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (not just a previous classification in ClinVar).
*   This code can be applied to an intronic or synonymous variant with the caveats below:
    *   Apply PS1\_Moderate for a variant predicted to disrupt splicing (SpliceAI score ≥0.2, meeting PP3) that is located outside the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions, if a comparison variant at the same nucleotide position, with the same predicted impact, has been classified likely pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
    *   Apply PS1\_Moderate for a variant predicted to disrupt splicing (SpliceAI score ≥0.2, meeting PP3) that is located outside the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions, if a comparison variant at a different position within the same splice region, with the same predicted impact, has been previously classified pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
    *   Apply PS1\_Moderate for a variant within the canonical splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions (meeting PVS1\_Strong / PVS1\_Moderate) if a comparison variant within the same splice donor/acceptor motif (but outside the +/-1,2 dinucleotide), with the same predicted impact, has been previously classified pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   This code can be applied to an intronic or synonymous variant with the caveats below:
    *   Apply PS1\_Supporting for a variant predicted to disrupt splicing (SpliceAI score ≥0.2, meeting PP3) that is located outside the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions, if a comparison variant within the same splice donor/acceptor motif, with the same predicted impact, has been classified likely pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
    *   Apply PS1\_Supporting for a variant located within the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions (meeting PVS1) if a comparison variant at the same nucleotide position or within the same donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide, with the same predicted impact, has been classified pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
    *   Apply PS1\_Supporting for a variant located within the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions (meeting PVS1) if a comparable variant within the same splice region, but outside the donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide, with the same predicted impact, has been classified pathogenic or likely pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
    *   Apply PS1\_Supporting  for a variant located within the splice donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide positions (meeting PVS1) if a comparison variant within the same splice region, but outside the donor/acceptor +/-1,2 dinucleotide, with the same predicted impact, has been classified likely pathogenic using the ClinGen Motile Ciliopathy VCEP’s rule specifications (PMID: 37352859).
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PS1

criteriaCodes.description:
Multiple lines of computational evidence suggest no impact on gene or gene product (conservation, evolutionary, splicing impact, etc)
Caveat: As many in silico algorithms use the same or very similar input for their predictions, each algorithm cannot be counted as an independent criterion. BP4 can be used only once in any evaluation of a variant.

evidenceStrengths.description: *   Apply BP4\_Strong for a missense variant if the REVEL score is less than or equal to 0.016 and the highest of the four delta scores within SpliceAI is below the cutoff of \<0.1.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description: *   Apply BP4\_Moderate for a missense variant if the REVEL score is less than or equal to 0.183 and the highest of the four delta scores within SpliceAI is below the cutoff of \<0.1.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Apply this code at default (BP4) strength for a missense variant if the REVEL score is less than or equal to 0.290 and the highest of the four delta scores within SpliceAI is below the cutoff of \<0.1.
*   Do not apply this code if the REVEL score is >0.290 or if the highest of the four SpliceAI delta scores is greater than or equal to 0.1
*   For a synonymous variant or an intronic variant outside of the canonical splice sites (+1, +2, -1, or -2), BP4 can be met if the highest of the four delta scores within SpliceAI is below the cutoff of \<0.1.
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: BP4

criteriaCodes.description: Allele frequency is above 5% in Exome Sequencing Project, 1000 Genomes or Exome Aggregation Consortium.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Met by Grpmax filtering allele frequency greater than or equal to 0.006 in gnomAD v4.1.1 or the most up-to-date version of gnomAD.
*   This threshold was calculated based on the Whiffen-Ware calculator, estimating the allele frequency at which 25% of the prevalence of the disorder (conservatively estimated at 1 in 10,000) could be explained by a single variant in a single gene, with 100% percent penetrance. Subsequent adjustment was made to ensure that the most frequent known disease-causing variant did not fall within the BS1 range.
evidenceStrengths.label: Stand Alone

criteriaCodes.label: BA1

criteriaCodes.description:
Well-established in vitro or in vivo functional studies supportive of a damaging effect on the gene or gene product.
Note: Functional studies that have been validated and shown to be reproducible and robust in a clinical diagnostic laboratory setting are considered the most well-established.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Please see the attached file entitled “DNAH5\_Functional\_Assays” for a description of all functional assays approved for use to meet the PS3 code.
*   Animal models with expression of a patient variant can meet PS3 at the default level but have not yet been found for _DNAH5_. Models have been identified for other PCD-related genes (for example a zebrafish rescue experiment with _CFAP298_ variants in PMID: 24094744, or a _CCDC103_ variant dimerization experiment in PMID: 28790179).
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   Please see the attached file entitled “DNAH5\_Functional\_Assays” for a description of all functional assays approved for use to meet the PS3 code.
*   Data from the following papers (showing splicing defects in patient cell RNA, which is preferred, or in mini-gene assays) can be used at PS3\_Supporting strength:
    *   Minigene assay - Failly et al. 2009 (PMID: 19357118)
    *   Patient RT-PCRs - Knowles et al. 2013 (PMID: 23261302)
*   The group considered making PS3\_Supporting applicable for patient cell assays with immunofluorescent staining of DNAH5 in ciliated cells or with electron microscopy showing outer dynein arm defects in ciliary axonemes (examples found in PMID: 16627867), but ultimately decided that these patient cell-based experiments should be included in the patient phenotype (PP4 code). This decision will be re-evaluated following a review of pilot data.
evidenceStrengths.label: Supporting

criteriaCodes.label: PS3

criteriaCodes.description: Located in a mutational hot spot and/or critical and well-established functional domain (e.g. active site of an enzyme) without benign variation.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   This code is met at the default level (PM1) by a missense, in-frame deletion, or in-frame insertion variant in residue 1980-1981, 1983-1987, 2005, 2028, or 2030-2033, which make up the ATP-binding sites (PMID: 32664073) that have been shown to be conserved among axonemal dyneins, and confirmed to lack known benign missense variation.
*   PM1 can be combined with PM5 and/or PP3, however, their combined strength is limited to strong. For example, a variant can meet both PM1 and PP3\_Moderate (which together are equivalent to 1 strong code), while a variant cannot meet PM1 in combination with PP3\_Strong.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate

evidenceStrengths.description:

*   Please note that these specifications are based on the domain locations listed below, which were obtained from the SMART database using the Pfam domain annotations (https://smart.embl.de/smart/show_motifs.pl?GENOMIC=1&DO_PFAM=DO_PFAM&INCLUDE_SIGNALP=INCLUDE_SIGNALP&ID=ENSP00000265104):

Note: This requires testing of parents (or offspring) to determine phase.

evidenceStrengths.description:

criteriaCodes.description: Variant found in a case with an alternate molecular basis for disease.
criteriaCodes.label: BP5

criteriaCodes.description:
Co-segregation with disease in multiple affected family members in a gene definitively known to cause the disease.
Note: May be used as stronger evidence with increasing segregation data.

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   This code is met at the PP1\_Strong level if the variant co-segregates with the affected phenotype across at least 3 segregations between the proband and similarly affected relative(s).
    *   Variant can be present in the homozygous / compound heterozygous state.
    *   In order to be considered “affected” the family member must meet group definition for PCD (consider age-based phenotypes). The family member must have; (1) An electron microscopy result showing a structural defect consistent with proband, or (2) situs inversus, or (3) wet cough from \<6 months of age combined with either chronic nasal congestion / neonatal respiratory distress / laterality defect, or (4) bronchiectasis combined with either chronic nasal congestion / neonatal respiratory distress / laterality defect.
    *   Please note that a segregation is counted for each familial connection between the proband and any similarly affected genotype-positive relative. For example, one segregation is counted for the connection to an affected sibling sharing the same genotype, or 3 segregations are counted for the connection to an affected first cousin sharing the same genotype.
    *   Known consanguinity may decrease the strength of this evidence.
    *   Segregations can be combined across multiple families.
evidenceStrengths.label: Strong

evidenceStrengths.description:
*   This code is met at the PP1\_Moderate level if the variant co-segregates with the affected phenotype across 2 segregations between the proband and similarly affected relative(s).
    *   Variant can be present in the homozygous / compound heterozygous state.
    *   In order to be considered “affected” the family member must meet group definition for PCD (consider age-based phenotypes). The family member must have; (1) An electron microscopy result showing a structural defect consistent with proband, or (2) situs inversus, or (3) wet cough from \<6 months of age combined with either chronic nasal congestion / neonatal respiratory distress / laterality defect, or (4) bronchiectasis combined with either chronic nasal congestion / neonatal respiratory distress / laterality defect.
    *   Please note that a segregation is counted for each familial connection between the proband and any similarly affected genotype-positive relative.     *   Known consanguinity may decrease the strength of this evidence.
    *   Segregations can be combined across multiple families.
evidenceStrengths.label: Moderate
